name: Ligaya Mishan
beat: NYC-focused restaurant criticism, with some national reach
note: NYT dropped critic anonymity with this appointment, so her identity is public; NYT also adds brief starred reviews from other writers.
ratingSystem: NYT stars, 0 to 4. Two stars means very good. Also Critic's Pick. Reviews nationwide. Writes the NYT 100 Best list.
howTheyDine: Not anonymous since June 2025. Multiple visits. Times calls for fact-check and photos about a month after a visit. Booking names and party size not published.
caresAbout: Imagination, ambience, service, technique, passion, commitment, deliciousness. Rewards places outside the usual fine-dining set (Caribbean Kabawa is No. 1 on her 2026 list).
recognizeBy: Dines openly; public photos exist. No published habits.
whyItMatters: Her stars are the most important review in New York.
relevanceToIara: NYC-based, covers all boroughs and global cuisines. No Brazilian review found.

recentReviews.verdict: Four stars. First NYT four stars outside NYC.
Four stars for kaiseki tasting menu.

name: Tejal Rao
beat: Nationwide restaurant criticism; California-based, travels often
note: Former NYT California critic (since 2018), James Beard award winner; no longer anonymous.
ratingSystem: NYT stars, 0 to 4, plus Critic's Pick.
howTheyDine: Not anonymous since June 2025. Based in California; reviews nationwide.
whyItMatters: Same star power as Mishan, but rarely in NYC.

name: Matthew Schneier
role: Chief restaurant critic (took over from Adam Platt, Aug 2023)
note: Former fashion/culture writer (The Cut, NYT) turned critic; reviews run on Grub Street.

photoCredit.text: Cultured magazine interview, cross-checked with Cultured group portrait

caresAbout: Recent pieces judged tasting menus (Cove, Saga) and the Babbo revival under Stephen Starr. Publishes a best-restaurants list.
whyItMatters: One of the last full-time critics in America. New York mag drives downtown buzz.

name: Helen Rosner
role: Food correspondent / staff writer; writes the Tables for Two restaurant column (took over from Hannah Goldfield by Sept 2025)
note: Won the 2024 James Beard Craig Claiborne Distinguished Criticism Award; ex-Eater and Saveur editor.
ratingSystem: No stars. Short Tables for Two column.
whyItMatters: Three-time James Beard winner, including for her restaurant column.
relevanceToIara: Writes Tables for Two on NYC restaurants.

name: Hannah Goldfield
role: Staff writer; former Tables for Two critic (first full-time New Yorker restaurant critic, 2018)
note: Stepped down from the Tables for Two column; Helen Rosner now writes it. Exact step-down date not verified.
whyItMatters: Departure not confirmed in this research.

name: Gwendal Poullennec
role: International Director of the MICHELIN Guides
beat: Oversees all Guide selections worldwide, including North America
note: The Guide's public face; inspectors themselves are anonymous. 2026 Northeast Cities ceremony (incl. NYC) is Dec 14 at the Glasshouse, Manhattan.

name: Michelin Guide inspectors (anonymous)
note: Book under assumed names and pay in full; cannot be identified by face or name. Treat every table equally.
ratingSystem: Stars by team consensus. Disagreement triggers more visits.
howTheyDine: Anonymous. Book under assumed names. Often dine alone. No notes at the table. Pay in full. May introduce themselves only after paying.
caresAbout: Ingredient quality, technique, harmony of flavors, the chef's personality on the plate, consistency across visits.
recognizeBy: No reliable tells. Do not guess.
whyItMatters: Stars or a Bib Gourmand change a restaurant's fate.
relevanceToIara: High. Consistency on every night is what they test.

name: Elazar Sontag
beat: National-profile critic based in DC; former Bon Appetit restaurant editor
note: Publicly shows his face and restored star ratings; still avoids reserving under his own name. Could visit NYC.
ratingSystem: Brought back WaPo stars. A counter-service spot can earn the same stars as fine dining.
howTheyDine: Not anonymous. Never books under his own name. Pays his own way. Multiple visits.
caresAbout: Whether a restaurant is the best version of itself.
recognizeBy: Dines openly. Former Bon Appetit restaurant editor.
whyItMatters: Ran Bon Appetit's Best New Restaurants list; national taste-maker.
relevanceToIara: Low for reviews (DC beat), but well known in NYC food circles.

name: Pete Wells
role: Reporter covering food (former chief restaurant critic, 2012 to Aug 2024)
note: Kept his face out of print for his whole run as critic, so there is no reliable photo. Booked under fake names.
howTheyDine: Three visits per review, each with three friends.
whyItMatters: Stepped down August 2024 for health reasons; still at the Times.

name: Florence Fabricant
role: Food and wine writer; Off the Menu column on new openings
beat: New restaurant openings and food news
note: Her Off the Menu column is where NYC openings get announced.
whyItMatters: Her opening column lists new restaurants; not verified in this research.

name: Eric Asimov
note: Likely to notice the wine program as much as the food.
whyItMatters: NYT wine voice; not verified in this research.

name: Priya Krishna
role: Food staff reporter; interim restaurant critic from July 2024
note: Filled in as critic alongside Melissa Clark after Wells. Whether she still reviews after June 2025 is unverified.
whyItMatters: NYT food coverage; not verified in this research.

name: Sam Sifton
role: Assistant managing editor; founder of NYT Cooking, former food editor
note: Influences NYT food coverage decisions. Exact 2026 portfolio unverified.

name: Ryan Sutton
role: Chief critic and editor; formerly Eater NY chief critic (position eliminated)
note: Longtime star-rating-style critic; now self-published, so he may dine on his own account.
recognizeBy: Keeps his face out of photos on purpose. Every published image hides it.
caresAbout: Restaurant economics and prices (for example sushi economics, slice pizza).
whyItMatters: Former Eater NY chief critic; his Substack is read by the industry.

name: Robert Sietsema
role: Independent writer; laid off from Eater Dec 2024, started Substack in 2025
beat: Cheap eats and neighborhood NYC dining
note: Decades-long NYC dining chronicler (ex-Village Voice, Eater) who writes about LES-type neighborhood places.
recognizeBy: Hides his face in photos (a devil mask, a camera). Treat any regular solo diner taking notes seriously.
caresAbout: Value and good food across all neighborhoods. Openings and neighborhood walks.
whyItMatters: 35+ years covering NYC; posts three times a week.
relevanceToIara: High. Covers openings and global food on a budget-to-mid range.

name: Stephanie Wu
role: Editor-in-chief (since March 2022); Eater now owned by PMX / Penske Media
note: Eater cut 15 staff in Aug 2025 incl. Northeast deputy editor Erika Adams; current Eater NY editor could not be verified.

name: Clare Reichenbach
beat: Runs the JBF Awards, JBF House and programs
note: Her organization names the Restaurant & Chef Awards (Rising Star, Best New Restaurant), which iara is eligible for after opening.

name: Jamila Robinson
beat: Leads both titles; Bon Appetit publishes the Best New Restaurants list
note: Former Philadelphia Inquirer food editor and ex-JBF journalism chair.

name: Hunter Lewis
beat: Leads F&W, incl. Best New Chefs
note: Runs the Best New Chefs program.

name: Morgan Carter
note: Ex-Denver food writer; leads Time Out NY's restaurant coverage.

name: Steve Cuozzo
role: Restaurant critic, real estate columnist (per Wikipedia, which lists him as living)
note: Veteran tabloid critic known for harsh pans. Whether he still reviews in 2026 is unverified. Still publishing at the Post as of Sept 2026.
whyItMatters: Longtime NY Post restaurant critic with a big mass audience.

name: Tom Sietsema
outlet: NOTUS / Next Course newsletter (formerly The Washington Post)
role: Food correspondent at NOTUS; retired as WaPo critic Oct 2025
note: 25 years as the Post's critic; famous for disguises and anonymity (now retired from that role).
howTheyDine: Tried to stay anonymous; revealed his face when he left in fall 2025.

name: Adam Platt
role: Former chief restaurant critic (22 years, to 2023); NYU journalism faculty
note: Reviewed NYC for New York magazine for 22 years before Matthew Schneier took over; not currently reviewing.
whyItMatters: Stepped down after 22 years; farewell essay I'm Full.

name: Ruth Reichl
outlet: Former NYT chief critic; Gourmet editor
role: Author and Substack writer; former NYT critic (1993-99) and Gourmet editor
note: Famous for wearing disguises while reviewing; still widely recognized in NYC.

name: Arthur Schwartz
outlet: Podcast (Food Maven / Food Mensch); formerly NY Daily News
role: Former NY Daily News restaurant critic and food editor; active podcaster in 2026
note: Longtime radio/podcast voice, still publishing 2026 episodes.

name: Keith Lee
beat: 10-point scale reviews, often takeout, favors Black- and family-owned spots
note: About 17M TikTok followers (May 2025); his visits create the 'Keith Lee effect' and he says he pays and has family pick up to avoid VIP treatment.
howTheyDine: Usually orders anonymously, often takeout, reviews in his car. Often with family.
caresAbout: Taste, how his family was treated, customer service, cost.
recognizeBy: Very famous face; millions of followers.
whyItMatters: One video can fill a dining room overnight.
relevanceToIara: Medium. NYC visits so far were mostly casual spots like pizza.

name: Dave Portnoy
note: One of the most visible NYC pizza reviewers by reach; role from general knowledge, not re-verified here.
ratingSystem: 0 to 10 decimal score, mostly pizza. Above 7 is respectable.
howTheyDine: Films a single-bite review, usually outside a pizzeria.
caresAbout: Crust, sauce, cheese, overall vibe. Leans New York thin crust.
recognizeBy: Famous face; often has a camera crew.
relevanceToIara: Low. iara is not a pizza shop.

name: David Chang
note: Industry heavyweight whose opinions travel; role from general knowledge, photo is from 2010.

name: Sonal Shah
note: She runs The Infatuation's New York coverage, including its new-bar and best-of guides.

name: Paolo Lucchesi
note: He leads Resy's editorial team, which publishes restaurant features read by Resy diners nationwide.

name: Beth Kracklauer
outlet: Freelance (formerly The Wall Street Journal Off Duty)
role: Freelance writer and editor; former WSJ Off Duty food and drinks editor (2012-2026)
note: She edited WSJ Off Duty food and drink coverage for over a decade and is now writing freelance, including for Outside in 2026.

name: Jay Cheshes
outlet: The Wall Street Journal / WSJ Magazine (contributor); Smithsonian
note: Former Gourmet New York critic and Time Out NY reviewer who still writes food features for the WSJ and, in 2026, Smithsonian.

name: Brad A. Johnson
outlet: Independent (frequent Robb Report contributor per his bio)
role: Food and travel writer and critic
note: James Beard Award-winning restaurant critic who published restaurant rankings in 2025 and is listed in his bio as a frequent Robb Report contributor.

name: Frank Bruni
outlet: Duke University / The New York Times Opinion
role: Patterson Professor of the Practice of Journalism and Public Policy at Duke; contributing Opinion writer at NYT
beat: Politics and culture (former NYT chief restaurant critic)
note: He was the NYT's chief restaurant critic before Sam Sifton and Pete Wells and is still a widely recognized food-world name.

name: Julia Moskin
beat: Restaurant industry, food news and investigations
note: Her March 2026 Noma investigation led to René Redzepi stepping down, and she shared a 2018 Pulitzer for restaurant-industry reporting.

name: Nick DiGiovanni
role: Chef and content creator (MasterChef S10 finalist)
note: He became YouTube's most-subscribed cooking creator in March 2026 and signed a Netflix content deal in July 2026.

name: Jeremy Jacobowitz
note: NYC food creator behind Brunch Boys who posts restaurant guides on Substack every week, most recently on Oct 5, 2026.

name: Brian Lindo
note: NYC food creator with 550K+ Instagram followers who covered the 2025 James Beard Awards and set a Guinness coffee-shop record in 2026.

name: Melissa McCart
beat: NYC restaurant news and dining reports
note: She runs Eater NY coverage and still files her own dining reports, including one dated Sept 23, 2026.

name: Alan Sytsma
beat: Oversees Grub Street and the magazine's best-new-restaurants coverage
note: He edits all of New York magazine's food coverage, including its annual best-new-restaurants list (discussed on TASTE, Dec 19, 2025).

name: Chris Crowley
beat: NYC restaurant reporting, openings, industry stories
note: He is New York magazine's senior food writer and covers new NYC openings (Beard Awards piece June 17, 2025; TASTE interview Nov 30, 2025).

name: Tammie Teclemariam
note: She writes New York magazine's Underground Gourmet review column (byline Oct 28, 2025), the slot most likely to cover an upscale-casual LES opening.

name: Bryan Kim
note: He leads The Infatuation's NYC editorial team and reviews restaurants himself (Cafe Charmant review, Sept 8, 2026).

name: Molly Fitzpatrick
note: She is a senior NYC reviewer for The Infatuation (review published Oct 1, 2026).

name: Will Hartman
note: He reviews NYC restaurants for The Infatuation (Table Mercato review, Oct 1, 2026).

name: Willa Moore
note: She reviews NYC restaurants for The Infatuation (Faux review, Sept 3, 2026).

name: Ellie Plass
note: She wrote Resy's feature on iara itself (Sept 25, 2026), so she may come in to follow up.

name: Kate Krader
note: She is Bloomberg's food editor and writes its global restaurant coverage (Pursuits newsletter, Feb 22, 2025).

name: Mahira Rivers
outlet: The New York Times (freelance) / Sweet City
role: Freelance restaurant critic; former Michelin inspector
beat: Restaurant reviews, NYC desserts (Sweet City newsletter)
note: She is a former anonymous Michelin inspector who now reviews NYC restaurants for the NYT (TASTE, Dec 19, 2025), so she is trained to dine without being noticed.
recognizeBy: Former anonymous Michelin inspector. Trained not to be noticed.

name: Melissa Clark
role: Food columnist, NYT Food and Cooking
beat: Recipes and home cooking; filled in on restaurant reviews in 2024
note: Longtime NYT food columnist; widely recognized from NYT Cooking videos.
